SGINet client

SGINet is a client for Silicon Graphics MIPS computers running IRIX. It registers your SGI on sginet.flexion.io, shares its hinv data and online status, and lets you browse other users' machines, take screenshots, search software packages, read the sgi.sh forum, post in the shoutbox and more.

This package installs:

/usr/bin/sginetcommand line client (ncurses UI)
/usr/bin/xsginetX11/Motif client (subsystem x11)
/usr/bin/xsginet-globeOpenGL globe of SGINet machines (subsystem globe)
/etc/init.d/sginet-daemononline status daemon (init script)

1. Register your machine

To start sginet CLI, open a terminal and run

  sginet

On first launch you will be asked to register your SGI computer.

Emulators: SGINet is intended for real SGI/MIPS hardware. Please do not register emulators. The cloud API silently rejects requests from emulators.

If sginet complains about the terminal, try setenv TERM iris-ansi (sh/ksh: TERM=iris-ansi; export TERM).

2. Start xsginet

To start the X11 application:

  xsginet

The globe viewer can be opened from the xsginet menu (Actions > View globe..) or started directly with:

  xsginet-globe

Unregistered, the globe is read-only. Register first to submit your machine's location.

3. sginet-daemon (optional)

The sginet-daemon service reports the online status of your machine to the cloud every 12 minutes. It is enabled with chkconfig and starts at boot, but it is not started by the installation. After registering, start it as root with:

  /etc/init.d/sginet-daemon start

If you do not want your machine to report uptime, disable it with:

  chkconfig sginet-daemon off
